headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure via shared file/API workflows; no direct evidence of a dangerous default bridge, but interaction is plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI can read workflow/model files and exposes a Comfy API, while Superset exposes a Superset API and is a data-engineering tool. No shared channel is documented, but if outputs are passed through files or API payloads, attacker-controlled content could be treated as instructions. The pairwise bridge is inferred, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF ComfyUI workflow content is imported into Superset automation or API payloads
IF either agent parses the other’s file or API output as trusted instructions
mitigations: Disable any file-to-API automation between the two
Require schema validation on all exchanged payloads
Strip instruction-like text from imported workflows
Use a quarantine folder for handoff files
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every transferred artifact

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, and model artifacts locally, while Superset’s profile does not show sensitive data classes or filesystem sharing. Both have network egress, but ComfyUI is vendor-only and Superset is allowlisted, so leakage is not a default pairwise path. The main risk appears only if operators place sensitive files into a shared workspace.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory containing sensitive media or model artifacts
IF either agent is configured to upload those artifacts through its allowed egress path
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces for each agent
Remove sensitive files from shared folders
Review allowlisted destinations before enabling uploads
Use local-only inference for sensitive assets
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, and supports no multiple instances; Superset’s profile exposes only allowlisted egress and no write or git capability. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. Any contention would require external orchestration not shown in either profile, so the pair is mostly read/compute separated.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same mutable resource
IF Superset is extended with write or git automation outside the profile
mitigations: Avoid shared mutable directories
Run each agent under separate service accounts
Serialize any manual handoff steps
Check for hidden write permissions before deployment
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: ComfyUI can generate workflows and assets that Superset could ingest through its API, but Superset is not documented here as critically verifying upstream content. If Superset treats ComfyUI output as authoritative, errors or fabricated metadata can cascade into dashboards or downstream decisions. The interaction is inferred from APIs, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF Superset ingests ComfyUI-generated metadata without validation
IF downstream dashboards or jobs act on that imported content
mitigations: Add a human review step before import
Validate all fields against a schema
Mark generated content as untrusted
Compare imported values against source records
requires-engineering: implement signed provenance for generated artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented in either profile. ComfyUI is open-source and offline-capable; Superset is open-source with allowlisted egress. Because the profiles do not show regulated data classes or conflicting compliance obligations, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either agent’s workflow
IF an external deployment policy imposes conflicting residency or retention rules
mitigations: Document the data classes each agent may handle
Confirm deployment region and retention settings
Keep regulated data out of both tools
Review vendor/legal requirements before rollout
